requirements.text: Fields with commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted and records end with CRLF
Cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return are neutralized so spreadsheets do not evaluate them
The file is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark (or another declared encoding) so Excel shows non-ASCII text correctly
The download is an attachment with a safe RFC 6266 filename, including non-ASCII names
Exports include only rows the requester may see in their tenant and only explicitly selected columns
Large exports are bounded or streamed (or run as a background job) instead of exhausting memory

evidence.name: RFC 4180: fields with commas, quotes and line breaks are quoted, quotes doubled, every record ends with CRLF
formula neutralization: = + - @ tab and CR prefixes get a leading apostrophe, then quoting applies
SQL: formula-like database text is neutralized and numeric columns come through; the export log records the run
Excel encoding: output is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark by default, CRLF records, and non-ASCII bytes intact
download headers: attachment with RFC 6266 filename and RFC 8187 filename* for non-ASCII names, text/csv, no-store
authorized rows: the row source is scoped to the requester
authorized rows: the authorize hook drops rows the requester cannot read and counts them as denied
SQL: schema applies; the row source returns only the requester
bounded export: maxRows stops the stream with limit-exceeded instead of silently truncating
bounded export: streaming applies backpressure, so an unread export fetches only a bounded number of pages
SQL: a row cap on a real table fails the stream and logs limit-exceeded

implementations.notes: Exports stream within the request (no background job); over-limit exports fail unless onLimit truncate is set. PGlite tests run on one connection.
